timingCorrection.reason: The original warm-session timing started after state hashing and planning, while other paths included more lifecycle work. Those cross-mode timing values were therefore not apples-to-apples.
timingCorrection.timerBoundary: outer wall-clock around complete run call; warm-session teardown excluded

modes.direct-cold: fixed direct route, rebuild only requested derived body each request
modes.ignition-cold: generic relevance/dependency route, rebuild requested body each request
modes.ignition-warm: generic route with persistent state-bound materialization cache
modes.eager-warm: materialize full capability body once and retain it

correctedMeasurements.interpretation: No memory advantage because every capability is relevant. The two warm modes are close enough that one hosted sample must not be treated as a universal speed winner.
Breadth eventually fills the Ignition cache to eager size. In this corrected hosted sample eager-warm was slightly faster overall.

strongestSupportedClaim: A state-bound warm materialization cache eliminates repeated reconstruction of still-valid derived state while preserving exact results. With equal wall-clock boundaries, warm Ignition becomes competitive or advantageous only after enough reuse amortizes routing/state-validation costs. Its memory advantage disappears once the touched capability set reaches the full body.
boundaries: Corrected timing values are still single hosted-run observations, not a statistical performance distribution.
Does not prove free compute, created RAM, or free energy.
Does not prove optimal cache eviction or partial invalidation.
Does not prove Ignition should replace direct or eager modes.
nextGate: Use the corrected timing boundary while testing an adaptive Governor, then eliminate avoidable orchestration work such as duplicate canonical-state fingerprinting before judging Governor performance.
